rules.applies_to: All tenant-scoped Ash resources and actions
rules.rationale: Fail-closed tenancy is the primary defense against cross-tenant leakage. Allowlisting global resources makes the only exception explicit, reviewable, and gateable.
rules.text: All tenant-scoped operations MUST execute with tenant set (fail-closed). Untenanted reads/writes are forbidden. The ONLY exception is an explicitly global resource allowlisted under /tenancy/global_resources/allowed_resources.

rules.rationale: Eliminates 'god mode by accident' and forces missing-tenant to be an explicit, testable failure.
rules.text: Any tenant-scoped Ash query/action executed without resolved tenant MUST raise Ash.Error.Invalid.TenantRequired; returning an empty set is forbidden.

rules.rationale: RLS is the hard guardrail preventing accidental cross-tenant reads/writes.
rules.text: Tenant-scoped tables MUST have RLS enabled and forced, and policies MUST restrict access to the tenant session variable app.current_org_id.

rules.applies_to: All app-role DB sessions for tenant-scoped operations
rules.rationale: SET LOCAL prevents tenant leakage across pooled connections and ensures scoping to the transaction.
rules.text: Tenant session variable name is locked to app.current_org_id and MUST be set using SET LOCAL inside a transaction.

rules.applies_to: All tenant-scoped tables and their indexes
rules.rationale: Prevents cross-tenant existence leakage via constraint violations and other integrity-check side channels.
rules.text: Tenant-scoped resources MUST NOT use globally-unique constraints/indexes on tenant-controlled or tenant-observable identifiers. All PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints for tenant-scoped tables MUST include org_id as the first column unless an explicit exception is granted.

rules.applies_to: Tenant-visible sequential numbering fields (e.g., ledger entry_seq)
rules.rationale: Prevents cross-tenant volume metadata leakage and enforces per-tenant deterministic sequencing.
rules.text: Global Postgres sequences MUST NOT be used to generate tenant-visible sequential numbers for tenant-scoped resources. Sequential numbering MUST be tenant-scoped (per org_id) and generated atomically under row lock (or equivalent) within the consuming transaction.

rules.rationale: Prevents cross-tenant references (confused deputy) and preserves tenant-partitioned join plans.
rules.text: Tenant-scoped relationships MUST use composite foreign key semantics including org_id (e.g., FOREIGN KEY (org_id, parent_id) REFERENCES parent (org_id, id)).

rules.applies_to: Non-audit, high-volume tables and internal IDs
rules.rationale: Avoids per-tenant hot-row lock contention while keeping strict sequencing for audit-critical, tenant-visible numbers.
rules.text: TenantSequence (row-lock allocator) MUST NOT be used for internal identifiers or high-volume log/telemetry/event tables where gaps are acceptable; use non-ordered identifiers (e.g., UUIDs) instead.

rules.rationale: Eliminates ambiguous 'global' exceptions that become security holes over time.
rules.text: A resource SHALL be considered global ONLY if it is listed in /tenancy/global_resources/allowed_resources. Absent an allowlist entry, the resource MUST be treated as tenant-scoped and MUST require org_id tenant context.

rules.rationale: Prevents global resources from becoming covert cross-tenant side channels.
rules.text: Global resources MUST NOT read, join, or aggregate tenant-scoped OLTP data. They MUST NOT contain org_id, tenant keys, or tenant-private fields, and MUST NOT provide query capabilities that can infer tenant existence or activity.

rules.rationale: Stops accidental tenant data leakage via shared caches and async workers.
rules.text: Any caching for global resources MUST be tenant-agnostic: cache keys and payloads MUST NOT include org_id or tenant-private data. Background jobs processing global resources MUST run without tenant context and MUST NOT touch tenant-scoped tables.

rules.applies_to: Phoenix PubSub topics and broadcast events used by Ticketing
rules.rationale: PubSub is a common accidental cross-tenant leak vector. Canonical topic partitioning also prevents real-time fanout storms by forcing event-scoped subscriptions for high-volume flows.
rules.text: All PubSub topics MUST be tenant-scoped by org_id and MUST follow the canonical Ticketing topic namespace patterns (org-scoped and event-scoped).

rules.applies_to: Rate limiting / throttling keys (Redis, ETS, DB-backed limiters) in Ticketing
rules.rationale: Without tenant-partitioned limiters, one org can degrade another by exhausting shared buckets or counters.
rules.text: All rate limit keys MUST be partitioned by org_id and MUST be namespaced under Ticketing to prevent cross-tenant interference.

rules.rationale: Returning ERR_FORBIDDEN for tenant mismatch leaks existence of resources in other tenants. ERR_NOT_FOUND is the only safe response.
rules.text: Tenant mismatch (TEN_TENANT_MISMATCH) and RLS denial (TEN_RLS_DENIED) MUST return ERR_NOT_FOUND at the top level to hide existence. API boundaries MUST NOT leak tenant isolation failures via FORBIDDEN semantics.

rationale: Prevents cross-tenant existence leakage and tampering by guessing/altering org identifiers.
Enables SEO slugs and WordPress-like flexible pages while keeping tenant isolation constitutional.
rules.text: Public/unlisted HTTP surfaces MUST resolve org_id via a server-generated opaque public_object_key. Client-supplied org_id via path/header/subdomain MUST NOT be accepted for public clients.

rules.applies_to: Platform-wide DSAR orchestration and any multi-org control-plane operations
rules.rationale: A platform control-plane needs to coordinate multi-org workflows (e.g., verified platform-wide DSAR) without granting blanket cross-tenant data access. This rule allows orchestration while preserving fail-closed tenant isolation for actual data access.
rules.text: A platform orchestrator MAY execute in tenant_scope="global_ops" with tenant unset ONLY for orchestration/control-plane work (e.g., scheduling per-org jobs, fleet coordination, capability/registry reads). It MUST NOT directly read or write org-scoped business resources unless it switches into an explicit tenant_scope="org" execution context for a single org_id (typically via per-org jobs). All global_ops execution MUST be capability-gated and fully audited.

rules.applies_to: Subject identifiers and link keys used across domains (PII vault, DSAR cases, tracking pseudonyms)
rules.rationale: Prevent silent cross-tenant linkage and enforce privacy boundaries (no PII in tracking, deterministic DSAR, and cryptoshred) without weakening tenancy isolation.
rules.text: Subject identifiers (subject_key and aliases) MUST be org_id-scoped. Cross-tenant subject linkage is forbidden by default. Any platform-wide subject processing MUST be explicitly scoped to a multi_org_scope list and MUST NOT rely on implicit global identifiers.

rules.applies_to: Any API/action that accepts correlation/group IDs that may span multiple orgs (e.g., checkout_group_id, provider_* ids)
rules.rationale: Prevents correlation identifiers from becoming an accidental cross-tenant authorization boundary (common source of leakage when multi-org checkout creates multiple org-scoped orders linked by a shared checkout_group_id).
rules.text: Tenant-spanning correlation identifiers (including checkout_group_id and payment/provider references) MUST NOT be used as an authorization boundary or as the sole query predicate for tenant-scoped resources. Any operation that accepts such identifiers MUST also enforce org_id tenancy (RLS) and actor capabilities; returned results MUST be filtered to the actor's authorized org_id scope.

For any HTTP/API surface operating on tenant-scoped resources with hide_existence enabled, the boundary response for unauthorized, cross-tenant, RLS-denied, tenant-mismatch, and missing-tenant MUST be indistinguishable from a genuine not-found: HTTP 404 with top-level code ERR_NOT_FOUND. Header sets MUST also be uniform for these outcomes (no WWW-Authenticate or tenant/policy headers).

When returning ERR_NOT_FOUND due to hide_existence, HTTP problem-details responses MUST NOT include the optional 'subcode' extension (ERR-1), and MUST NOT vary any response fields based on the hidden reason. If 'detail' is present, it MUST be a constant generic string (or omitted) for all ERR_NOT_FOUND outcomes.

summary: Constitutional tenancy rules for a multi-tenant Ash 3.x platform: explicit tenant propagation, strict fail-closed execution, Postgres RLS with transaction-scoped tenant session state, index isolation to prevent cross-tenant existence leaks via integrity checks, and tenant-scoped sequencing for tenant-visible ordered numbers.

allowed_tenant_setting_methods.name: tenant: option passed to Ash calls

fail_closed_behavior.notes: Any tenant-scoped Ash query/action executed without resolved tenant MUST raise TenantRequired; returning an empty set is forbidden.

notes: Tenant is REQUIRED for tenant-scoped resources. Do not set `global? true` on Ash resources unless explicitly permitted by TEN-1 global_resources allowlist.
For globally-unique identities across tenants, use Ash identity option `all_tenants?: true` and document the exception in TEN-1-RULE-005.

background_jobs.notes: Jobs MUST carry org_id explicitly in args and set tenant at job start.
background_jobs.tenant_set_policy: Jobs MUST set tenant context before calling any tenant-scoped domain_actions; tenant context MUST be org_id and MUST be fail-closed.

cache.notes: All tenant-varying cache keys MUST include org_id and MUST be namespaced under the Ticketing prefix to prevent cross-app collisions.

constraints: When tenant is unset, the orchestrator MUST NOT read or write tenant-scoped resources.
The orchestrator MUST spawn per-org execution jobs that set tenant to each org_id before any tenant-scoped access.
Platform-wide orchestration MUST include an explicit multi_org_scope list and MUST be capability-gated (see IAM-1) with strict verification evidence (see DSAR-1).

tenant_spanning_correlation_ids.definition: Identifiers used only for correlation/grouping or external reconciliation and that may span multiple orgs.
notes: Example: checkout_group_id may link multiple org-scoped orders created from a single checkout session. It MUST NOT grant cross-org visibility; clients may only see orders they are authorized to read within each org_id.

pubsub_topics.notes: Tier 2 event-scoped topics are REQUIRED for high-volume real-time flows (e.g. seating holds) to prevent org-wide fanout storms.

rate_limiting.notes: All throttling buckets MUST be tenant-isolated; a single org MUST NOT be able to exhaust another org's limiter capacity.

cross_tenant_oltp_aggregation.reason: Forbidden in OLTP; only audited offline analytics may aggregate.

global_resources.definition: A resource is 'explicitly global' ONLY if it is listed in tenancy.global_resources.allowed_resources. If this allowlist is empty, then there are no global resources and all reads/writes are tenant-scoped and MUST be denied without org_id.
implementation_notes: Prefer compile-time/static enumerations for truly global reference data (e.g., ISO codes).
If persisted, global resources MUST be schema-isolated and MUST NOT reference tenant tables via foreign keys.

notes: This policy is about boundary safety. Internal diagnostics MAY retain stable tenancy subcodes for logs/jobs.
Any surface that uses hide_existence MUST return the same problem-details shape as a genuine not-found, without subcode, to prevent tenant enumeration.
For tenant-scoped resource operations, missing tenant context MUST be treated as existence-hidden at the boundary.

allowed_only_when: The unique field is an unguessable, server-generated identifier and is never client-supplied.
The unique constraint is not tenant-observable at any boundary (errors are masked and audited).

session_variable.name: app.current_org_id
session_variable.notes: Tenant context MUST be transaction-scoped to avoid leakage across pooled connections. The org_id type is UUIDv7 per Ticketing constitutional requirement for time-ordered, distributed identifiers.

notes: PII vault mappings (subject_key<->identity aliases) MUST be keyed by org_id.
Cryptoshred MUST destroy aliases and link keys inside each org_id boundary without mutating immutable truth records.

hard_constraints: When tenant is unset, the orchestrator MUST NOT read or write tenant-scoped resources.
The orchestrator MUST spawn per-org execution jobs that set tenant to each org_id before any tenant-scoped access.
Platform-wide orchestration MUST include an explicit multi_org_scope list and MUST be capability-gated (see IAM-1) with strict verification evidence (see DSAR-1).

notes: subject_key is a pseudonymous subject identifier that MUST be interpreted within an org_id boundary.
Cross-tenant linkage of a subject is forbidden unless explicitly orchestrated as a platform-wide DSAR with an explicit multi_org_scope list.

recommended_implementation.atomic_update_sql: UPDATE tenant_sequences SET next_val = next_val + 1 WHERE org_id = $1 AND sequence_name = $2 RETURNING next_val
recommended_implementation.notes: Sequence allocation MUST occur inside the same transaction as the write that consumes the number.

notes: When profile_id=public_surface, ignore actor_claim for tenant selection. Authorization is still enforced by resource visibility checks and IAM policies where applicable.

when_multiple_sources_present_and_disagr.notes: Treat as authorization boundary failure; do not leak which tenant is correct.

notes: Tenant MUST NOT be set until the actor is proven to be a member of that org (or is a system-internal caller explicitly permitted by policy). Membership validation semantics are defined in IAM-1.
Default profile for authenticated admin/backoffice and service-to-service calls.
Public/unlisted event browsing and checkout initiation MUST resolve tenant only via public_object_key.
actor_claim MUST NOT be used to select tenant for public surfaces; do not force users to log out to browse other orgs' public pages.
Preferred tenant source: the authenticated actor's org_id claim.
Do not accept tenant headers from browsers/mobile apps.
Headers may be used only in internal service-to-service traffic or behind a trusted gateway that authenticates the actor and injects the correct org_id.
Public/unlisted surfaces MUST resolve tenant via an opaque public key, not via org_id in URL/subdomain/header.
Slug segments are SEO-only and MUST NEVER influence tenant or resource resolution; mismatch triggers canonical redirect only.
If an authenticated actor is present, public_object_key resolution MAY override actor_claim ONLY for public/unlisted read or checkout initiation boundaries.
Path parameters may be used only in backoffice/admin routing where membership/role is verified before tenant is set.
Subdomain routing MUST NOT be used for unauthenticated public access. Membership validation is required for all subdomain-based tenant resolution.

definitions.description: Org-scoped execution. org_id MUST be present and MUST be the active tenant for all data access, pricing, inventory, ledgers, and policy evaluation.
Platform/global operational execution (orchestration only). MUST NOT read/write org-scoped business resources without switching into an explicit org scope; MUST be capability-gated and auditable.

determinism_rules: Entry points MUST explicitly declare tenant_scope for every request/job/action context; implicit or ambient scope MUST NOT be assumed.
If tenant_scope == "org": org_id MUST be present and tenant resolution MUST succeed; failures MUST be treated as access denial (fail-closed).

If tenant_scope == "global_ops": org_id MUST NOT be present in the request context, and the active tenant MUST be unset. Any per-org work MUST be executed by spawning org-scoped jobs with explicit org_id.
security_notes: global_ops MUST NOT leak tenant existence; error mapping MUST follow TEN-1 leakage posture (uniform not-found/forbidden patterns).
global_ops is NOT a license for cross-tenant reads; it exists only for orchestration/ops control planes.
